# ISSUE-27 implementation plan

Give the signed-in DEEP FIELD BBS a door directory and ship Relay Trivia as its first entry. Both JSON and reviewed TypeScript doors use the same host. Players can leave a door, keep their checkpoint, and see a completion acknowledgement on the board. The approved profile is detailed. The work is estimated at 12–18 hours for planning, implementation and validation, within the 32-hour claim budget. The plan has a human review gate.

## What we know

- DEEP FIELD unlocks on Episode 000 completion. The hub offers CONNECT and the BBS model already handles sign-in, the farewell, SYSOP, and disconnect. The terminal supports typed commands and menu buttons with text-only rendering. [Board](../../content/bbs/deep-field.json#L3) · [Bootstrap](../../src/main.ts#L103) · [BBS dispatch](../../src/bbs/bbs.ts#L140) · [Terminal](../../src/terminal/terminal.ts#L58)
- Save v2 isolates JSON door slots from global fields and already discards individually malformed encoded slots. The existing codec leaves door-specific version and shape checks to the consumer. It also refuses writes to future saves. [Save codec](../../src/progress/save.ts#L110) · [Save session](../../src/progress/save.ts#L184) · [Save regressions](../../tests/unit/save.test.ts#L210)
- The Node reader and Vite browser glob discover JSON recursively. The CLI and Vite content plugin both call loadContent, which already records source locations, checks duplicate IDs, collects grantable flags, and validates conditions and grants. [Node reader](../../src/content/node.ts#L5) · [Browser reader](../../src/content/browser.ts#L3) · [CLI](../../scripts/validate-content.ts#L5) · [Build plugin](../../scripts/content-plugin.ts#L6) · [Reference checker](../../src/content/validate.ts#L153)
- GitHub Actions already runs the Playwright suite on Linux with Node 24 and Chromium. Playwright discovers tests under tests/e2e and builds dist in global setup. The fixture serves the Pages subpath through request interception. [Workflow](../../.github/workflows/browser-tests.yml#L11) · [Playwright config](../../playwright.config.ts#L5) · [Global setup](../../tests/e2e/global-setup.ts#L3) · [Fixture](../../tests/e2e/fixtures.ts#L16)
- The task snapshot has the BBS and save prerequisites from the dependent issues. The checked-in architecture still directs authors of door games to the hub tool list. [BBS model](../../src/bbs/bbs.ts#L13) · [Save slots](../../src/progress/save.ts#L52) · [Architecture](../../docs/architecture.md#L37)

## What we're assuming

- Use a short two-question equipment practice quiz with all clues on its own screens. Give it the proposed stable ID relay-trivia, gate it on Episode 000 completion, and acknowledge completion with a board-only flag and menu line. Check the copy and fact references against the existing board and story during step 4.
- One labelled BBS terminal can host the additional screens. Check focus, command submission, and return on the actual production build in step 5. Use the completed-v1 fixture to place the keyboard test at the start of the BBS milestone.
- This release ships a JSON door. Prove the reviewed TypeScript route with test-only implementations and a failing module; the production code-door list is initially empty.

## Open questions

- The planner's native Linux role has source access and no Chromium capability. The production keyboard result and the size of the new entry bundle will be observed in step 5 by the existing Browser tests workflow. Native review can verify the route, tests and fixture wiring.
- Only the configured Linux native/Codex path and GitHub Actions Ubuntu/Chromium path are in this plan. Other Swarm backends, harnesses, operating systems and browser engines are unmeasured. The production path is the static Vite build at the existing Pages subpath. Evidence for the native paths is in .swarm/config.yaml:4–6,16–18,59–67 and package.json:8–18. Evidence for the browser path is in .github/workflows/browser-tests.yml:11–25 and tests/e2e/fixtures.ts:16–37.

## Implementation

1. **Define the contract and validate registrations.** In new src/doors/contract.ts, document and type the common descriptor, lifecycle and host-facing screen/result. Descriptors contain id, name, description, author via required attribution, positive integer version, a requires condition, declared rewards and returnTo (bbs-menu for this release). Lifecycle implementations declare a save-state schema and completion rule, and implement launch, input, save, restore and exit. Give callbacks a frozen progress view with only a fact query backed by a detached snapshot and their own working state. Return plain screen text and actions for host rendering. Provide a typed way to adapt door-specific state to the common registry boundary. Keep door callbacks and storage access independently testable in Node.
   - Add doorMetadataSchema, triviaDoorSchema and Content.doors in src/content/schema.ts. Use the existing ID, attribution, condition and fact formats. The strict trivia variant declares a saveState kind selecting the built-in trivia index validator, completion as all questions answered correctly, and authored prompts, options, feedback and completion lines. Validate that each answer index identifies a real option and report the indexed field. Add optional BBS board status entries containing a condition and text, defaulting to an empty array for old boards.
   - Add new src/doors/code-doors.ts with an explicit typed CODE_DOORS list of static metadata, source labels and literal lazy import callbacks. An entry owns its metadata and loads only the trusted lifecycle module bundled from its literal import path. Validation reads metadata without invoking callbacks. In src/content/validate.ts, add the doors kind and initializer, parse code metadata from the same catalog, and reject door ID collisions across JSON and code. Keep JSON records in the content manifest. In checkReferences, collect declared rewards from both kinds before validating references. Validate door entry conditions and indexed reward facts, and board status conditions. Use the same source-map diagnostics for invalid metadata, cross-kind collisions and bad references.
   - Add new src/doors/registry.ts with createDoorRegistry and lookup/list behavior. Register both types in a single ID namespace and reject collisions without replacement. Snapshot host-owned metadata, including the reward list, before calling any implementation. Use src/content/conditions.ts:15 for entry checks in both listing and launching. Registering and listing code door metadata performs no module evaluation. Verify with the registration and content cases in TEST_PLAN.md.
2. **Host lifecycle and state.** Add createDoorHost in new src/doors/host.ts, built around the existing SaveData, factsOf, addFact and persist callback at src/progress/save.ts:52,208,226,234. Provide launch by ID, input and exit, with results the BBS can render. Gate launches using current facts. Look up the active ID's own property, with a versioned envelope inside that slot. Decode and validate version and payload with the door's schema before restore. For absent, wrong-version or schema-invalid slots, run fresh launch. The next successful checkpoint replaces the bad slot. Keep Save v2 and its encoded object-of-JSON-strings representation.
   - Run the callbacks and validate and detach any save payload before changing progress. After successful input or exit, checkpoint only the active slot. Evaluate the declared completion rule on validated state and apply the registered reward list idempotently through the host. Completion on the final answer is saved before reporting success. Use a single persist call for slot and reward facts. Preserve the previous slot and facts if commit fails. Pass neither the save record, a slot selector, storage callbacks, nor grant functions to implementations. Expose read-only fact queries, and detach door state and metadata across the interface so retained references cannot change committed progress. Completion returns a signal to the host, which selects the registered facts.
   - Catch code module evaluation/load failures and exceptions in launch, input, save, restore, exit and completion/validation. Clear the active door, report a typed failure to the BBS, and retain the prior checkpoint and global progress. An invalid slot is identified before restore and starts fresh. A restore exception for a schema-valid payload returns to the board with the same error path used by the other lifecycle failures. Add a test-only lazy module in tests/fixtures/throwing-door.ts whose top-level evaluation throws. Verify start/menu availability before selecting it, failed selection, and successful play of another door on the same board.
3. **Connect the host to the BBS.** In src/bbs/bbs.ts, extend createBbs, screen and dispatch with a signed-in DOORS directory, OPEN <id> actions and a return-to-main-menu transition. Keep the existing sign-in, SYSOP, read effects and disconnect contract. Supply live entry options and facts to the BBS model. List only launchable IDs, and feed typed and selected OPEN commands through the same launch gate. Display the eligible status entries on main-menu entry, including after return from a door and when reconnecting after reload.
   - Add new src/bbs/door-session.ts with createBbsDoorSession to resolve OPEN asynchronously and route commands to the active lifecycle. Use EXIT for a normal save and return to the signed-in menu. Route failures through the same return transition and display a brief authored board system line (for example, "DOOR CARRIER LOST. BACK AT DEEP FIELD."). Source this copy from the board record using an optional door-error field with a generic system fallback for existing board fixtures. Serialize transitions while a lazy load is pending. Keep the underlying BBS dispatch synchronous for its existing callers. The browser and BBS integration tests use the same session controller.
   - Wire the registry and host to the existing save session in src/main.ts and pass a BBS door session to createBbsScene in src/bbs/bbs-view.ts. Reuse the current terminal renderer and BBS> prompt through door entry and return. Give play options the same keyboard and button paths, restore prompt focus after each transition, and ignore delayed UI updates after scene disposal. The hub's puzzle tool list stays in src/app/tools.ts.
4. **Ship content and document the contract.** Add new content/doors/relay-trivia.json and new src/doors/trivia.ts with createTriviaDoor. Use numbered choices, deterministic answer checking, a retry hint, and a saved question index bounded by the question count. Use a JSON-defined completion rule, with the validated final index as its result. Opened completed sessions show completion and EXIT. Declare flag:relay-trivia-complete as the optional reward and add a board-only status such as RELAY DRILL: COMPLETE in content/bbs/deep-field.json. Add the board's error copy in that record. Keep text and answer data in JSON. Verify a fresh player can solve the quiz from its own copy and that no Episode 000 or later required story condition consumes the flag. Replace the door extension guidance in docs/architecture.md and add the module and ownership boundaries, lifecycle and save/recovery rules, and registration paths. Keep the existing puzzle tool guidance. The three main doors, authoring guide and starter template are out of scope.
5. **Prove the journey.** Add tests/unit/doors.test.ts for the pure registry, lifecycle and BBS session integration. Extend tests/unit/content.test.ts and tests/unit/bbs.test.ts for discovery, diagnostics and compatible BBS behavior. Update tests/unit/helpers.ts for Content.doors. Extend tests/e2e/bbs.spec.ts with the full keyboard milestone, using the existing one-time save seed and production fixture. Verify signed-in return, visible reward, and read/completion persistence on a genuine reload. See TEST_PLAN.md for commands and ownership.

## HANDOFF

Verify these anchors against the approved source. This handoff describes design and evidence. Approved inputs and validation remain owned by the workflow.

| Area | Entry points and symbols |
| --- | --- |
| Content | src/content/schema.ts:4–33 (shared primitives), :141 (bbsBoardSchema), :230 (Content); src/content/validate.ts:44 (SCHEMAS), :63 (loadContent), :134 (checkDuplicates), :153 (checkReferences), :247 (formatErrors) |
| Door runtime | New contract.ts, registry.ts, code-doors.ts, trivia.ts and host.ts under src/doors. Boundary is createDoorRegistry → createDoorHost → createBbsDoorSession. Evaluate entry with src/content/conditions.ts:15 and reuse the save functions at src/progress/save.ts:110,125,208,226,234. |
| Board and browser | src/bbs/bbs.ts:59 (createBbs), :67 (screen), :140 (dispatch); new src/bbs/door-session.ts; src/bbs/bbs-view.ts:11 (createBbsScene), :28 (run), :84–91 (mount/dispose); src/main.ts:20–31 (content and save), :106–135 (CONNECT); src/terminal/terminal.ts:58–107 (command routing, text rendering, focus) |
| Authored data and docs | New content/doors/relay-trivia.json; content/bbs/deep-field.json:3–18; docs/architecture.md:5–18,37–42 |

Extend tests/unit/content.test.ts:144,264,294,368 for schemas, collisions, references and CLI output. Reuse the temporary-copy pattern at tests/unit/bbs.test.ts:132 and the in-memory storage pattern at tests/unit/save.test.ts:17. Keep the slot corruption and migration regressions at tests/unit/save.test.ts:155,210,243. Extend the migrated keyboard journey at tests/e2e/bbs.spec.ts:13–56 using tests/e2e/helpers.ts:5 and tests/fixtures/episode-000-complete-v1.json.

Focused commands are below. CI owns the browser run.

- `npm test -- tests/unit/doors.test.ts tests/unit/bbs.test.ts tests/unit/content.test.ts tests/unit/save.test.ts tests/unit/episode.test.ts tests/unit/links.test.ts`
- `npm run content:validate`
- `npm exec --offline -- prettier --check src/doors src/bbs src/content/schema.ts src/content/validate.ts src/main.ts content/doors content/bbs/deep-field.json docs/architecture.md tests/unit/{doors,bbs,content}.test.ts tests/unit/helpers.ts tests/fixtures/throwing-door.ts tests/e2e/bbs.spec.ts`
- `npm exec --offline -- eslint src/doors src/bbs src/content/schema.ts src/content/validate.ts src/main.ts tests/unit/{doors,bbs,content}.test.ts tests/unit/helpers.ts tests/fixtures/throwing-door.ts tests/e2e/bbs.spec.ts`
- `npm exec --offline -- tsc --noEmit`
- `npm run test:e2e` in Browser tests. A CI-side diagnostic can target `npm run test:e2e -- tests/e2e/bbs.spec.ts`.

The approved source snapshot was checked with find and file existence tests. All nine planned new source, content and test files are absent there. The snapshot excludes Git metadata. Grep confirmed the schema's typed empty-content fixture, the BBS entry point, and the exact architecture wording. Reading the codec, recursive loaders, and workflow confirmed the save, discovery, and CI assumptions. Reopen if the approved base lacks those prerequisites, the tested production import path requires eager evaluation of optional code, the proposed checkpoint cannot preserve other progress, or meeting acceptance would require changing protected workflow files or authoring story-required mechanics.

**What this change breaks**

| Located dependency | Planned handling |
| --- | --- |
| src/main.ts:123 is the single production caller of createBbsScene | Update its session wiring. Preserve CONNECT availability and return to the hub on DISCONNECT. |
| tests/unit/bbs.test.ts:27–46 asserts sign-in/menu actions and exact message labels | Assert DOORS in the configured signed-in menu. Preserve the existing actions, message indices, read-only-once effects and login prompt contract. |
| tests/e2e/bbs.spec.ts:25–135 depends on BBS> focus, SYSOP copy, designation, handle and READ status; tests/e2e/episode.spec.ts:37 depends on the existing gate | Extend the keyboard milestone and preserve those assertions and the pre-Episode gate. |
| tests/unit/helpers.ts:3 constructs Content, consumed by tests/unit/dialogue.test.ts:85 | Add doors: [] to the helper. Preserve the dialogue fixture behavior. |
| tests/unit/content.test.ts:164,183,205,394 asserts manifest shape, schema version and a single-record synthetic CLI run; docs/architecture.md:31 describes the shared pipeline | Add door manifest coverage. Preserve the schema version, JSON manifest shape and existing diagnostics. The new optional board fields keep existing JSON valid. |
| tests/unit/save.test.ts:155,210,243 and tests/fixtures/episode-000-complete-v1.json cover independent BBS/door progress, corrupt slots and old/future saves | Preserve the codec, fixtures, version and existing regression assertions. |
| docs/architecture.md:42 ties doors to src/app/tools.ts; :24 describes puzzle tools; tests/unit/links.test.ts:18 checks relative documentation links | Replace the door guidance. Preserve the puzzle explanation and ensure added code links resolve. |
| docs/game-design.md:163–171 describes the later doors; docs/content-authoring.md and .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE propose existing transmission and archive flows | Preserve unchanged. No door-authoring template consumes this contract in the approved snapshot. |

# ISSUE-27 test plan

The eight rows follow the approved WorkUnit order. Developer checks run in the configured native Linux Codex harness with Node 24 and Vitest. Browser execution uses GitHub Actions Ubuntu and Playwright Chromium against the static Pages build. The independent tester reviews all eight criteria and reuses applicable command evidence.

## Acceptance coverage

| # | WorkUnit criterion | Observable cases and verification |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Tests cover registration, duplicate-id rejection, entry requirements, launch, exit, save, and restore across a simulated reload | In tests/unit/doors.test.ts, register JSON and lazy TypeScript definitions; reject repeated IDs across both types and within either type, preserving the initial registration. Check list and direct launch with unmet and met requirements. Launch, answer one question, exit, reopen from the same serialized storage with a fresh save session and door host, and verify restore continues at the next prompt. Confirm no reward before completion. Run D1. |
| 2 | Tests prove a door can't change global progress except through its declared rewards, and can't read or write another door's slot | In tests/unit/doors.test.ts, seed two independent state slots and unrelated global fields. Drive a test implementation through the public host, check the immutable fact-query surface, try to attach an extra fact or target slot via untyped callback output, and mutate retained working state and save references after checkpoint. Verify its inputs never contain the storage or the second door's sentinel and that the second slot is byte-for-byte unchanged after save and reload. Assert incomplete input and exit issue no reward and that successful completion issues the original declared facts once, even after re-entry and reload. Inspect the registry snapshot and host commit path for bypasses. Run D1. |
| 3 | When a test door throws during launch, input, save or restore, the player returns to the BBS with a diegetic error, and global progress is intact | In tests/unit/doors.test.ts, use the production createBbsDoorSession with faulting test lifecycles. Parameterize launch, input, save and restore separately. Trigger restore with valid versioned state and trigger save after an input that would otherwise complete. Each failure returns the signed-in main menu with the authored board error; subsequent MESSAGES/HELP works. Compare persisted bytes and in-memory global progress, the previous checkpoint and another door's slot with their pre-failure values. Also verify failed persistence leaves no partial reward or state commit. Run D1. |
| 4 | A door with broken saved state restarts safely instead of blocking the BBS, and a throwing optional door module doesn't stop the game from starting | In tests/unit/doors.test.ts, independently seed invalid slot JSON, a wrong door version and valid JSON with invalid door-specific state; check fresh prompt, unchanged unrelated slots and globals, and a valid replacement on the next checkpoint. Register a literal lazy import of tests/fixtures/throwing-door.ts through the same registry path used by the app. Assert startup and board commands work before selecting it, selection yields the authored error and menu, and another door works immediately afterward. Preserve the existing codec corruption test. Verify bootstrap uses the tested registry without eager evaluation. Run D1. |
| 5 | A new declarative door can be added by adding one JSON file, demonstrated by a test on a temporary content copy; `npm run content:validate` reports bad door files with file and field | In tests/unit/content.test.ts, copy the real content tree, add one JSON door with a unique ID and no edits to the board or registry, then validate, confirm its manifest source and open/play it via the regular registry and BBS directory. In separate negative cases verify malformed JSON → (file), out-of-range answer → questions.0.answer, duplicate ID → id, unresolved entry requirement → requires, and a non-flag reward pointing to a nonexistent record → rewards.0. Verify a flag granted by JSON or code metadata is accepted by checkReferences when a BBS status consumes it, and that a misspelled condition is rejected at the indexed status field. Use the existing CLI subprocess pattern for a bad door, assert exit 1 and the emitted file and field. Run D1 and D2; reproduce from any invalid copy with `npm run content:validate -- /path/to/copied-content`. |
| 6 | Completing the first door changes something visible in the BBS through a declared reward, and it persists after a reload | In tests/unit/doors.test.ts, drive the actual RELAY TRIVIA content through the BBS session, checking the status line is absent before completing or after an early exit, visible on return after completion, and visible on reconnect using a new session from persisted bytes. Verify the saved reward is the declared flag and the door-local completion still restores. Assert the status condition is backed by that flag. Browser check C1 independently observes the same visible change on the built site. Run D1, D2 and C1 under their listed owners. |
| 7 | A browser test in the `Browser tests` workflow plays the whole milestone by keyboard: enter, read a message, meet SYSOP, finish the door, return, reload, and confirm the progress kept | Extend tests/e2e/bbs.spec.ts's migrated keyboard journey. Seed the completed Episode 000 v1 fixture once. Use Enter to join and typed commands with Enter to connect, use designation, open MESSAGES and READ 1, return to MENU, view SYSOP, open DOORS and OPEN relay-trivia, answer the authored questions and EXIT. Assert screen-specific output, BBS focus, the prior absence and post-return presence of the board acknowledgement, and return without another sign-in. Reload once without re-seeding, join and reconnect by keyboard, and confirm the acknowledgement and LAST ONE OUT [READ]. Reopen the completed door to demonstrate the saved local state. Keep existing disconnect/custom handle coverage. Run C1; Playwright discovers the spec through the existing config. |
| 8 | `docs/architecture.md` replaces the "tool in `src/app/tools.ts`" door guidance with this contract | T1 checks the extension section and links against implemented entry points. Verify the module boundary, JSON and explicit trusted code registry path, launch/input/save/restore/exit, read-only fact view, scoped state, declared rewards, and return/failure behavior. Confirm the legacy "A new door game or instrument" guidance is gone and the existing puzzle tool reference remains. Run D1 for documentation links and D3 for formatting. |

## Developer-owned focused checks

- **D1** Run `npm test -- tests/unit/doors.test.ts tests/unit/bbs.test.ts tests/unit/content.test.ts tests/unit/save.test.ts tests/unit/episode.test.ts tests/unit/links.test.ts`. The existing tests/unit/content.test.ts:368–413 helper redirects child process output to files and already exercises the CLI/build integration. Use that pattern for the new errors. Keep temporary-tree mutations within the test's temp directory.
- **D2** Run `npm run content:validate` on the actual content to exercise the same validation as the temporary-tree test. The production shell script uses the optional positional content root.
- **D3** Run focused format and ESLint checks and package type checking. This checks changed files and the TypeScript wiring, including the added Playwright spec.

```bash
npm exec --offline -- prettier --check src/doors src/bbs src/content/schema.ts src/content/validate.ts src/main.ts content/doors content/bbs/deep-field.json docs/architecture.md tests/unit/{doors,bbs,content}.test.ts tests/unit/helpers.ts tests/fixtures/throwing-door.ts tests/e2e/bbs.spec.ts
npm exec --offline -- eslint src/doors src/bbs src/content/schema.ts src/content/validate.ts src/main.ts tests/unit/{doors,bbs,content}.test.ts tests/unit/helpers.ts tests/fixtures/throwing-door.ts tests/e2e/bbs.spec.ts
npm exec --offline -- tsc --noEmit
```

Each developer command is estimated at under 5 minutes with prepared dependencies. Record exact commands, exit status, elapsed time, applicable acceptance evidence, and source identity in IMPLEMENTATION.md. Keep raw logs in the role's TMPDIR. Use a commit and clean-tree verification when available, or record a SHA-256 digest of the checked source snapshot including changed and new files, content, tests, lockfile and tool configuration. The source identity must allow the tester to confirm reuse against the final candidate.

## Tester-owned independent review

- **T1** Read the final diff or snapshot and map each acceptance row to actual implementation and test assertions. Check the registry is the same one used by the browser and the shared validator, that only literal imports declared by source review can load modules, that startup reads only their metadata, that the host owns every mutation, and that board text and reward gates are data-backed. Inspect tests for real serialized reload, separate fault cases and the real lazy module failure. For documentation, run `sed -n '5,75p' docs/architecture.md` and follow module references. The final review should also confirm the milestone uses only intended keyboard actions and the existing CI discovery path.
- Reuse D1–D3 results from IMPLEMENTATION.md when commands, inputs and final source identity match. Record the reference, applicability and reuse decision in VALIDATION.md. Rerun only an affected file or focused static/format check for relevant changes, an observed failure or unresolved coverage, documenting the reason and outcome. Reuse the browser job for C1 on the corresponding source identity when it exists. If it has yet to run and the native environment cannot run Chromium, record the external environment in the acceptance evidence for criterion 7. Use the unit evidence for criterion 6's save/reload behavior and record the browser observation when available.
- Record provisional results per the compiled tester instructions, including the exact ordered acceptance text and evidence references in the machine-readable acceptance block. A missing native result stays unverified until applicable evidence exists. Agent observations remain advisory and cannot satisfy claim-bound validation or publication.

## CI-owned browser check

- **C1** The existing Browser tests job installs dependencies and Chromium and runs `npm run test:e2e`; global setup builds first. For a failure that needs a narrow CI-side reproduction, run `npm run test:e2e -- tests/e2e/bbs.spec.ts` in a Chromium-capable job. The checked-in workflow and Playwright configuration already cover the added assertions. Use the job's visible results, including the milestone and existing bundle-budget test, as evidence for the tested revision. Native agents have no Chromium execution path.

## Coordinator-owned reference policy and longer checks

The coordinator runs the complete trusted-base policy in .swarm/validation/required-checks.yaml once after roles finish and before publication. The full policy includes format, lint, build and unit tests with its own setup and timeouts. Agent results provide advisory observations. The policy source, attestation and publication remain coordinator-owned.

| Command or check | Sole owner | Estimated duration | Evidence and later reuse |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Complete trusted-base required policy, including `npm ci --prefer-offline --no-audit --no-fund && npm test` | coordinator | Roughly 5–20 minutes for the complete policy, with approved 5-minute timeouts for format, lint and build and 15 minutes for the unit policy entry | Coordinator validation record and authoritative VALIDATION.md tied to the final candidate and trusted policy revision. Publication uses its claim-bound result. Other roles read the record when available. |
| Browser tests job through `npm run test:e2e`, including built-site keyboard milestone and bundle budgets | CI | Roughly 5–15 minutes including setup, with the existing 30-minute job timeout | GitHub Actions job log and per-test results for the tested commit or PR merge commit. Match the tested tree to the final candidate before reuse. Tester and maintainer reuse that evidence for browser coverage and review. |
